section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes a single daily-diary study of college women examining how within-person and between-person levels of self-compassion moderate the effects of interactions with body-focused others on body appreciation, intuitive eating, body image concerns, and affect. It highlights that higher-than-usual or generally higher self-compassion buffered or reversed negative associations with body-focused interactions and notes this is the first known daily study of women's frequency of such interactions.
section_summary.evidence_source: "The present study tested the hypothesis that among college women..."; "On days when college women were less self-compassionate than usual, more frequent daily interactions with body-focused others was associated with less intuitive eating and body appreciation, and more body image concerns and negative affect."; "This was the first study to our knowledge to examine women's self-reported frequency of interactions with body-focused others on a daily basis..."
